paper_title: A Spectroscopic Search for Optical Emission Lines from Dark Matter Decay
coupling_convention: two-photon decay rate Gamma in s^-1 exactly as plotted on the y-axis of Fig. 8 (NOT converted to g_agamma; paper relates them via Gamma = g^2 m^3 / 64 pi in natural units)
notes: DESI stacked dark-sky spectra search for narrow optical emission lines from DM two-photon decay around BGS/LRG galaxies (~50 kpc impact parameter). Main result (Fig. 8) is a bound on the decay rate Gamma [s^-1] vs particle mass, derived from a 5-sigma surface-brightness detection limit of 1e-19 erg/s/cm^2/arcsec^2 over 2000-9000 A. The paper states the constraint corresponds to particle lifetime > 3e25 s (Gamma < ~3.3e-26 s^-1) over the mass range 5-12 eV, which I encode as a flat two-point bound. The exact Gamma(m) curve is only in Fig. 8 (machine-readable data on Zenodo, not in text). The ALP interpretation uses Gamma = g^2 m^3/(64 pi), so the bound maps to g_agamma ~ 1.6e-12 to 6e-12 GeV^-1 over 12-5 eV. No local DM density assumed (extragalactic halo bound via weak-lensing surface mass density). Paper quotes a 5-sigma detection limit rather than a 90/95% CL; 0.95 is a conservative placeholder.
